title: Academic career planning and leadership (ACLA) course 2026-2027 – apply now, deadline 10.9.
content:
The seventh edition of the Academic career planning and leadership course (ACLA) is now open for applicants (deadline 10.9.2026 at 15:00). This course is targeted to post-doctoral researchers who are launching their independent researcher career and are thinking about building their own research group.

We will discuss career planning and trajectories, strategic mapping of research horizons, funding opportunities/challenges, building and leading a research group, project management, social impact issues and publication strategies, data management and research ethics. 

Approximately 15-20 participants will be enrolled, representing a wide disciplinary range of social sciences and humanities, across all faculties of the City Centre Campus.

The course will convene in six sessions (Fridays: 10-15) over the academic year.

Workshop days are: October 9 (warm-up session), October 23, November 20, December 11, January 22, February 19, March 19, and April 16.

Participants should make sure that they are able to commit to these dates.

For early May (2027) we are planning an excursion to Brussels to learn about European science policy and funding opportunities.

title: Helsinki Education Hub Joins "To Finnish Education and Beyond" Podcast Series
content:
Over the course of the series, the podcast speaks with researchers, entrepreneurs, ecosystem builders, and public sector operators who are shaping the future of education in Finland and beyond.

In the first episode, our Project Manager Heidi Lammassaari and Senior Business Advisor Niko Lindholm talk about why the intersection of research, entrepreneurship, schools, and innovation matters more than ever. Collaboration isn't a nice extra anymore. It's a requirement if we want to build educational innovations that actually work in everyday life.

content:

title: Kielipankissa: Rodolfo Basile
content:
I am an Italian linguist whose career began with the Finnish language. At the University of Naples ”L’Orientale”, I studied Finnish Language and Literature as my main subject at both bachelor’s and master’s level. I also studied German as a minor and improved my Swedish language skills during an Erasmus exchange at the University of Helsinki. In Helsinki, I worked as a teaching assistant in Italian and Finnish language courses. After completing my master’s degree, I joined FILI (Finnish Literature Exchange) in Helsinki as a trainee through the Finnish in Finland training programme funded by the Finnish National Agency for Education.

In 2024, I completed my PhD in Finnic Languages jointly at the Universities of Tartu and Turku under a cotutelle agreement. During my doctoral studies, I also taught Finnish. After earning my PhD, I moved to Kyoto, Japan, to work as a postdoctoral researcher.

title: BGA 2026 Newsflash
content:
took place in Amsterdam on June 23rd-26th, 2026. BGA, founded in 1970, is an international society dedicated to the scientific study of the interrelationships between genetic mechanisms and behaviour (human and animal), education/training of researchers, and public dissemination of knowledge on genetics and behaviour and their implications for health, development, and education. Overall, BGA 2026 showcased the field’s integration of classical twin/family methods with large-scale genomic, multi-omics, and causal-inference approaches, while highlighting early-career researchers and the societal/public dimensions of behavioural genetics research. 

Dr. Li Tian from the CLIPI group participated in a ” in the BGA 2026 conference. She gave an oral presentation on the recent research findings of direct and indirect parental genetic effects of neuropsychiatric predisposition on child’s externalizing and internalizing behavioural problems using family-based trio datasets in a multi-cohort study.

title: Co‑Creating Field Expertise: Strengthening Herpetological Skills with Emerging Liberian Scientists
content: Herpetological research in West Africa has historically been spatially and temporally patchy, leaving many areas understudied and local ecological knowledge underrepresented in scientific literature. In response, the GCC Lab and the University of Liberia have launched a collaborative initiative focused on strengthening practical field skills among undergraduate biology students. Through hands‑on training and mentorship, participants develop competencies in sampling methods, species identification, and field safety, while also contributing with their local knowledge and perspectives. The program emphasizes mutual learning and aims to support the development of future Liberian scientists equipped to lead conservation efforts in their own country.
